title: Staggered decommission triggered cross-region backpressure and variant fallback surge — post-incident analysis
creator: Ana Martinez
summary: A staggered node decommission in Region EU-C triggered unexpected cross-region backpressure. The routing control plane misaligned compatibility mappings for an older variant name, causing a rapid escalation to higher-tier fallback variants and exhausting reserved capacity for Dedicated customers. This document contains timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, and follow-ups.
impact_summary: Traffic spiked to fallback model variants in NA and APAC as EU-C began staggered decommissioning. Latency increased 3-5x for P99 on affected routes, error rates rose to 8% for a 14-minute window. Two Dedicated customers observed degraded throughput and were switched to lower SLAs automatically.
detection: Automated routing-threshold alerts (Routing SLO Monitor) followed by two customer support tickets reporting timeouts. Observability graph showed rapid increase in fallback-variant calls and queue growth in NA region.
timeline: 2025-02-18T03:05:12Z - Automated alert: per-region queue depth for EU-C > 75th percentile and drain initiated
2025-02-18T03:07:40Z - Control plane started staggered decommission plan (rolling drain with 30s offset between AZs)
2025-02-18T03:08:10Z - Compatibility mapping service returned mixed model variant keys for compatibility hash v3.2 (race between cache TTL refresh and decommission tags)
2025-02-18T03:10:02Z - Smart router applied fallback policy: prefer same-tier variants across regions; due to mapping mismatch, requests were routed to higher-tier fallback variants in NA and APAC
2025-02-18T03:11:30Z - NA Dedicated pool reached 92% utilization; autoscale didn't trigger because reserved capacity policy disallowed burst; latency P99 degraded
2025-02-18T03:12:45Z - Support tickets created by two Dedicated customers; engineering pager triggered
2025-02-18T03:18:00Z - Emergency rollback: paused decommission and forced per-request variant pinning to last-known-compatible variant; traffic rebalanced
2025-02-18T03:27:50Z - Error rates and latency returned to baseline after 9 minutes from rollback; full verification complete 03:35Z
root_cause: Three interacting failures: 1) A staggered decommission schedule used short offsets between AZ drains which amplified transient inflight rebalancing; 2) Compatibility-mapping TTL refresh raced with decommission metadata, producing inconsistent variant keys across control-plane replicas; 3) Fallback policy logic favored cross-region availability over strict variant compatibility, causing escalation to higher-tier variants and concentrated load on a small set of Dedicated pools.
mitigations_short_term: Paused the rolling decommission within 4 minutes of alert
Applied an emergency control-plane directive to pin requests to last-known-compatible variant hash for 30 minutes
Temporarily loosened Dedicated burst restrictions for affected accounts to allow fallback consumption without hard throttles
Deployed hotfix to compatibility-mapping cache to use stronger invalidation on decommission events (cache TTL 60s -> immediate tombstone update)
Notified impacted customers and opened remediation credits where appropriate
mitigations_long_term: Change default decommission choreography to use synchronized epoch-aligned drains with explicit global quiesce windows rather than short stagger offsets
Revise compatibility-mapping semantics so that decommission events write tombstones that are majority-acked before routing decisions (stronger consistency for variant mapping)
Update fallback policy to prefer variant compatibility first, then tier/cost heuristics; introduce dynamic caps on cross-region fallback volume
Add a routing-simulator unit to CI that replays decommission events against live mapping caches to detect race conditions
Extend Dedicated autoscale policy to allow short emergency bursts for cross-region pressure scenarios with billing guardrails

notes: Avoid ultra-short stagger offsets for high-traffic regions; small offsets turned small transient imbalances into systemic pressure
Control-plane cache invalidation must treat decommission as a critical path event
Customer impact was amplified by Dedicated burst policy which prioritized isolation over resilience; trade-off review required
Communication: improve pre-decommission runbook and add customer-visible maintenance banners for reserved customers
